originalAlarm.description: Potential leak of memory pointed to by '__ch_1934'

sanitizedDescription: Potential leak of memory pointed to by 'ch'
reasoning: TRUE POSITIVE (CORRECTLY CONSTRAINED): bc0ffc0e971.c (BusyBox nameif). 'Potential leak of memory pointed to by ch' at line 43. In the cleanup loop, 'delete_eth_table(ch)' frees both 'ch->ifname' and 'ch' at each iteration. The next iteration sets 'ch = ch->next', which is a use-after-free on the already-freed 'ch'. This corrupts the traversal — the analyzer reports a potential memory leak because subsequent list elements may not be properly freed after the use-after-free corrupts the 'ch->next' read. Same underlying bug as TRANSFORMATION_34 (use-after-free at line 43) and TRANSFORMATION_5 (double-free at line 15 inside delete_eth_table). CORRECTLY CONSTRAINED: ENABLE_FEATURE_CLEAN_UP=true is required since the for loop and delete_eth_table calls are inside '#ifdef ENABLE_FEATURE_CLEAN_UP'. The STRICT_ANSI variants cancel out.
